routes.label: Set up your AdvisorTrack portal account

rules.title: Financial Advisors do advisor work in Advisor Workspace and Android
rules.statement: Financial Advisors do their own book of business in Advisor Workspace on the web (/advisor) and in the Android app. A Financial Advisor who also holds Organisation Administrator permission may use organisation/account administration in the Management Portal; it does not grant leadership reporting scope. Ordinary Financial Advisors do not use Team Pipeline, Advisors, company Production, or Performance in the Management Portal.

rules.title: Organisation Admin is not a reporting rank
rules.statement: Organisation Administrator is not a reporting rank. It is a company-scoped grant stored separately from Executive, Regional Manager, Team Leader, and Financial Advisor, and it is not users.role. It does not replace hierarchy-controlled reporting scope.

rules.title: Reporting scope remains hierarchy-controlled
rules.statement: Visibility and writes are resolved server-side from reporting lines: Executive → Regional Manager → Team Leader → Financial Advisor. Clients must not supply authorised user IDs. Organisation Admin does not expand reporting scope to the whole company for pipeline or production.

rules.title: Purchased / Assigned / Available licence meaning
rules.statement: Purchased is the company’s operational seat pool (companies.seat_limit). Assigned is the number of currently licensed members. Available is Purchased minus Assigned, or Unlimited when Purchased is unlimited. Assigning a licence consumes Available. Removing a licence returns it to Available. Purchased does not change when a licence is assigned or removed.

rules.title: Additional licence requests need AdvisorTrack confirmation
rules.statement: Customers request extra licences from Licences. The request does not increase Purchased until AdvisorTrack confirms it according to the company’s contract workflow. Do not tell customers to use the internal Licence Requests queue.

rules.title: No hard deletion of business history
rules.statement: AdvisorTrack does not hard-delete customer business records as a cleanup strategy. Use deactivate, revoke, expire, archive, or supersede. Removing a licence or deactivating a user retains advisor data.

rules.title: Invoice numbers start at INV100000
rules.statement: AdvisorTrack invoice numbers are INV100000 and increment by one. They are unique, sequential, and never reused.

rules.title: AdvisorTrack is not currently VAT registered
rules.statement: AdvisorTrack is not currently registered for VAT. Customer invoices must not add VAT, imply VAT included, or print an AdvisorTrack VAT number. The on-screen label is “VAT not charged”. Charging VAT is a future configuration change, not a customer setting.

rules.title: Last Mobile Activity is Android resource telemetry only
rules.statement: Last Mobile Activity is Android resource telemetry. It records when the mobile app last used AdvisorTrack resources. It must never be described as productivity, performance, attendance, or how hard an advisor is working. An empty value is not inactivity.

rules.title: Licence assignment requires Available licences
rules.statement: A licence cannot be assigned when Available is 0. The portal then prompts to request additional licences. Do not exceed the purchased pool.

cards.title: Portal versus Android
questionForms: What is the difference between the portal and the mobile app?
Where should I sign in?
cards.summary: The Management Portal is for leadership reporting and for Organisation Administrators. Financial Advisors do their own book in Advisor Workspace (/advisor) and in the Android app. A Financial Advisor who is also Organisation Administrator may use organisation/account administration in the portal; that grant is not leadership reporting scope. Portal users set a password from an activation email.

cards.title: Who uses the Management Portal
aliases: who can log into the dashboard
questionForms: Who uses the Management Portal?
Can my advisors use the web dashboard?
cards.summary: Executives, Regional Managers, and Team Leaders use the Management Portal for reporting and organisation work. Organisation Administrators use it for users, licences, subscription, and invoices even if they are not a leadership rank. Financial Advisors use Advisor Workspace for their own book; Organisation Admin is a separate portal grant and does not add reporting scope.

cards.title: Who uses the mobile app
questionForms: Who uses the mobile app?
Where do advisors work?
cards.summary: Financial Advisors use Advisor Workspace on the web and the AdvisorTrack Android app for their own pipeline, contacts, and production. Organisation Admin does not move that advisor work into Management reporting. Last Mobile Activity on advisor details is Android resource telemetry, not a productivity score, and web Advisor Workspace use does not update it.

cards.title: Account activation
questionForms: How do I activate my account?
I received an invitation email, what do I do?
cards.summary: Portal users open the invitation link, then use Set up your AdvisorTrack portal account to choose a password (at least 8 characters, with a letter and a number). Financial Advisors activate on the Android app, not this page. Organisation Administrators always activate on the portal.

steps.label: Choose a password on Set up your AdvisorTrack portal account
Sign in to the Management Portal

cards.title: Forgot password
questionForms: How do I reset my password?
I forgot my password
cards.summary: On Sign in, choose Forgot password? Enter the email for your AdvisorTrack account. If an account exists, AdvisorTrack emails the same six-digit code used by the Android app. Codes expire after one hour. Enter the code, then choose a new password with at least 8 characters, a letter, and a number. The page does not say whether an email is registered. There is no reset link and no different token.

steps.label: Open Sign in and choose Forgot password?
Enter your email, then the 6-digit code from the email
Choose a new password and return to Sign in

cards.title: Advisor Home
aliases: how do I read my dashboard
questionForms: How do I read my dashboard?
What does my Home page show?
cards.summary: Advisor Home is your self-scoped book of business, not the Management Dashboard. It shows monthly progress, weekly activity, a pipeline snapshot of this month’s completed stage outcomes, and upcoming activities from your own records. Figures come from the same advisor dashboard, planning targets, and subscription APIs used by Android. You cannot open another advisor’s Home.

cards.title: Monthly progress
questionForms: How is my monthly progress calculated?
What is issued production?
What is potential production?
cards.summary: Monthly progress uses your nett goal from Planning. Issued is this month’s production dated by due date or created date, where the entry is issued or the application status is Accepted / Issued. Potential (estimated) is all of this month’s production on that same date rule, plus estimated commission on open cases that are not linked to production. Progress % is issued versus the monthly nett goal. Home issued can differ from Management Production because that page uses a different period basis — Advisor Home follows the existing Home contract and does not mix the two.

cards.title: Weekly activity and points
questionForms: What are weekly points?
Why are weekly points locked?
Why is something locked?
cards.summary: Weekly activity shows this week’s completed Calls, Meetings, Quotes/Analysis, and Submissions against your planning targets, plus weekly points earned versus the weekly point target. Those tiles come from the advisor dashboard, not invented frontend maths. If weekly points or another Home tile is locked, your current plan does not include that feature — the page shows the genuine locked state from subscription. Open Subscription / Plan in Advisor Workspace to see your plan.

cards.title: Pipeline snapshot
questionForms: What does the pipeline snapshot show?
What are the six pipeline stages?
Why is Interview shown as Fact-finding?
cards.summary: The Home pipeline snapshot is this month’s completed activity outcomes for your book, not the Management Team Pipeline. The six displayed stages are Initial contact, Fact-finding, Analysis & quotes, Recommendation, Implementation, and Review & servicing. The database and API may still store Fact-finding as Interview; the web label is Fact-finding. Conversion percentages are proceeded versus lost at each stage for the month. If pipeline analytics are not on your plan, the snapshot is locked.

cards.title: Upcoming activities
questionForms: What are upcoming activities?
cards.summary: Upcoming activities are your own scheduled follow-ups and case next-action dates in the next 30 days. Home shows time, type, title, contact when the API supplies it, and stage. Tapping a row opens Activities. If upcoming events are not on your plan, the list is locked. Home does not create or complete activities.

cards.title: Set my monthly target
questionForms: How do I set my target?
cards.summary: Your monthly nett goal is stored on your advisor planning profile and shown on Home as the Monthly Progress target. Open Planning & Targets in Advisor Workspace to set or change it. Home does not calculate a different goal. Until a goal is set, Monthly Progress explains that no monthly nett goal is set yet.

cards.title: Add a contact
questionForms: How do I add a contact?
What information do I need to add a contact?
cards.summary: Open Contacts in Advisor Workspace and choose Add Contact. First name is required, and you must also enter an email or a phone number. Last name, company, status, priority, rating, notes, and POPIA consent are optional. The stored statuses are Prospect, Active, Inactive, and Client — not lead, hot lead, qualified, or converted. Saving a contact also opens a case for that person. You only see your own contacts.

steps.label: Enter first name and an email or phone number

cards.title: Email or phone is required
questionForms: Why do I need an email or phone number?
cards.summary: AdvisorTrack will not save a contact without a first name and at least one of email or phone. That is the same Android and API rule. You do not need both. Search still uses name and company only — entering an email or phone does not add extra search fields.

cards.title: Edit a contact
questionForms: How do I edit this contact?
How do I edit a contact?
cards.summary: Open the contact and choose Edit. You can change the same API-supported fields used on Android: name, email, phone, company, status, priority, rating, and notes. Practice contacts stay editable. Archived real contacts on free or Live Preview plans are read-only until you activate a slot or upgrade to Pro. The API returns the actual restriction, such as CONTACT_ARCHIVED or LIVE_PREVIEW_REQUIRED — not a generic save failure.

cards.title: Search contacts
questionForms: How do I search for a contact?
cards.summary: Use the search box on Contacts. Search matches first name, last name, and company through the existing contacts API. It does not search email or phone. You cannot invent extra server filters. Results stay limited to your own book.

cards.title: Contact status
questionForms: What does this contact's status mean?
cards.summary: Canonical contact statuses are Prospect, Active, Inactive, and Client. Prospect is the default for a new contact. Inactive may follow a Lost activity outcome. Client is set when production income is recognised or issued. People may say “lead” in conversation; that is not a stored AdvisorTrack status. Priority and rating are separate from status.

cards.title: Prospect
questionForms: What does Prospect mean?
cards.summary: Prospect is the default contact status when you add someone. It means they are in your book and not yet a recognised client. It is not a separate CRM stage such as lead, hot lead, or qualified.

cards.title: Client
questionForms: What does Client mean?
cards.summary: Client is the contact status used when production income for that person is recognised or issued. It is not a manual “converted” label you invent. If a prospect became a client, look at issued or recognised production linked to that contact.

cards.title: Inactive
questionForms: What does Inactive mean?
cards.summary: Inactive is a contact status. It may result from an activity outcome of Lost. It is not the same as an archived Live Preview slot. Archived is activation state on a real contact; Inactive is the contact status field.

cards.title: Contact priority
questionForms: What is priority?
cards.summary: Priority is Low, Medium, or High on the contact. It is independent of status and of rating. Changing priority does not turn a prospect into a client.

cards.title: Contact rating
questionForms: What is contact rating?
cards.summary: Rating is a 0 to 5 value on the contact. It is your own ranking, separate from Prospect / Inactive / Client status and separate from Low / Medium / High priority.

cards.title: POPIA consent
questionForms: What is POPIA consent?
cards.summary: POPIA consent is the attestation that you may keep this person’s details. On Add Contact you can record consent. Import requires consentAccepted true and writes a POPIA audit entry without extra client PII. The contact then shows when consent was recorded. This is personal-contact POPIA handling, not Organisation Bulk User Import.

cards.title: Add Activity from a contact
questionForms: How do I create an activity?
How do I create an activity for a contact?
cards.summary: Open the contact and choose Add Activity. Title, type, the contact, and scheduled time are required. Duration, description, and pipeline stage are optional. This uses POST /activities with the same fields as Android. Saved activities also appear on Activities and on Home upcoming.

steps.label: Enter title, type, and scheduled time

cards.title: Open Case
questionForms: How do I open a case?
How do I start/open a case?
cards.summary: Open the contact and choose Open Case. AdvisorTrack loads or creates the open case for that contact through GET /cases/contact/:contactId. Do not create a second case from the browser. That same case opens at /advisor/cases/:caseId. Pipeline is your own book at /advisor/pipeline, not Team Pipeline.

cards.title: A case opens when you add a contact
questionForms: Why was a case created when I added a contact?
cards.summary: When you add a contact, AdvisorTrack automatically creates an open case for that person. That is the existing Android/backend side effect. Import does not create cases the same way; use Open Case, which get-or-creates the case. Do not add a second case from the web form.

cards.title: Import contacts
questionForms: How do I import contacts?
How many contacts can I import?
cards.summary: Import on Contacts sends 1 to 50 structured contact rows to POST /contacts/import with consentAccepted true. It is a Pro entitlement. It is not Organisation Bulk User Import and not an XLSX workbook. Duplicates are skipped by email/phone fingerprint. Practice/Live Preview limits still apply to real contacts after import.

steps.label: Enter up to 50 rows and confirm POPIA consent

cards.title: Live Preview
questionForms: What is Live Preview?
What is the three-contact limit?
Why can't I add another real contact?
cards.summary: Live Preview is a personal Android/advisor subscription option, not a company licence seat pool. On Live Preview you may keep up to 3 active real contacts. Practice contacts are excluded from that cap. If Live Preview is off, enable it or upgrade to Pro before adding real clients. CONTACT_LIMIT_REACHED means the 3 active real slots are full. Company licence counts do not appear on Advisor Contacts.

cards.title: Activate a contact slot
questionForms: What happens when I activate another contact?
cards.summary: POST /contacts/:id/activate moves an archived real contact into an active Live Preview slot. If you already have 3 active real contacts, the oldest active real contact is archived so the new one can take the slot. Practice contacts are not part of that swap. Pro users are not capped at 3.

cards.title: Practice contact versus real contact
questionForms: What's the difference between a practice contact and a real contact?
cards.summary: Practice contacts are sandbox people for learning. They do not count toward the Live Preview limit of 3 active real contacts. Real contacts are your actual book and use Live Preview or Pro entitlements. Company licence seats are a different product and are not shown on Advisor Contacts.

cards.title: Delete a contact
questionForms: Can I delete a contact?
cards.summary: The current Android/backend contact API still hard-deletes a single contact after confirmation. Web Contacts offers the same Delete with a warning that linked activities, cases, and production may be affected by existing database relationships. There is no bulk delete on this page. This is current contract behaviour, not a new retention design.

cards.title: Add an activity
questionForms: How do I add an activity?
How do I create an activity from a contact?
cards.summary: Open Activities and choose New Activity, or open a contact and choose Add Activity. Title, type, and scheduled date and time are required. Contact, duration, description, and pipeline stage are optional. Types are Call, Meeting, Email, Follow-up, Presentation, and Other. The same create form is used from Contacts and from Activities — one activity row, not a second task system.

steps.label: Enter title, type, and scheduled time

cards.title: Follow-up
questionForms: How do I schedule a follow-up?
What does Follow-up mean?
cards.summary: Follow-up is a normal activity type (`follow_up`), not a separate database. Use it when the next action is a follow-up. Today, upcoming, and overdue lists still come from Activities. Asking the Assistant about “follow-ups today” counts this type; asking about “activities today” counts all scheduled types.

cards.title: Edit an activity
questionForms: How do I reschedule an activity?
How do I edit an activity?
cards.summary: Open the activity and choose Edit. You can change title, scheduled date and time, description, and status using the existing PATCH fields. Type, contact, duration, and pipeline stage are set at create and are not part of the current PATCH contract. After save, the page uses the server response rather than guessing.

steps.label: Change the supported fields and save

cards.title: Complete an activity
questionForms: How do I complete an activity?
What does Complete do?
cards.summary: Open the activity and choose Complete / Record Outcome, then Complete. Complete records the outcome as completed and does not automatically create the next activity. You may optionally advance the open case to the next pipeline stage (`advanceCase`). If the activity is at Implementation, or you choose submit to production with a valid amount, the backend may submit the open case to production. The web does not create a second production row.

cards.title: Proceed
questionForms: What does Proceed do?
What happens when I choose Proceed?
When is the next activity created?
Why was another activity created automatically?
How do Activities affect my pipeline?
cards.summary: Proceed records the outcome as proceeded and creates the next activity at the next pipeline stage. The default next time is tomorrow at 11:00 unless you override it. Stage-to-type mapping is owned by the backend (Initial contact → call, Fact-finding/Interview → meeting, Analysis → follow-up, Recommendation → presentation, Implementation → other, Review → follow-up). The open case is moved to that next stage. There is no next stage after Review — the API returns NO_NEXT_STAGE. Do not recreate this mapping in the browser.

cards.title: Lost
questionForms: What happens if I choose Lost?
What does Lost do?
What happens when I mark an activity Lost?
Why did my prospect become inactive?
Why did my case become Lost?
cards.summary: Lost records the outcome as lost. If the activity has a contact, that contact becomes Inactive and any open case for that contact becomes lost. Confirm before you continue — the web warning tells you this will happen. Lost does not create a next activity. Current product does not offer an undo for this side effect.

steps.label: Read the Lost warning, then confirm

cards.title: Activity types
questionForms: What activity types are available?
cards.summary: The product types are call, meeting, email, follow_up, presentation, and other. The web shows Call, Meeting, Email, Follow-up, Presentation, and Other. There are no extra desktop-only types.

cards.title: Overdue activity
questionForms: What is an overdue activity?
cards.summary: An activity is overdue when its scheduled date and time is earlier than now and its status is still scheduled. Completed or cancelled activities are not overdue. Dates use Africa/Johannesburg. Being created earlier does not make an activity overdue.

cards.title: Delete an activity
questionForms: Can I delete an activity?
cards.summary: The current Android activity API hard-deletes an activity. Web mirrors that with a confirmation that the activity will be permanently removed. There is no bulk delete and no archive conversion in this phase. Restoring a deleted activity is not available. This is the same future retention product debt as contact delete.

cards.title: My Pipeline
questionForms: What is my pipeline?
Where is my pipeline?
cards.summary: My Pipeline at /advisor/pipeline is your own book of cases. It is not Team Pipeline and not a leadership downline view. Cases come from GET /cases using the authenticated advisor identity. You cannot list another advisor’s cases. Open a card to work the case at /advisor/cases/:caseId.

cards.title: The six pipeline stages
questionForms: What are the six pipeline stages?
What are the six stages?
cards.summary: The canonical advice journey has six stages: Initial contact, Fact-finding, Analysis & quotes, Recommendation, Implementation, and Review & servicing. Desktop Pipeline uses those labels. Do not invent extra stages.

cards.title: Initial contact
questionForms: What happens in Initial contact?
cards.summary: Initial contact is the first pipeline stage. Capture the contact, start the case, send the document checklist items, and set a next action if you want one. FICA is not required at this stage. A next action is optional.

cards.title: Fact-finding
questionForms: What happens in Fact-finding?
cards.summary: Fact-finding is where you record a simple goal or a full FNA. Moving into or past this stage with incomplete FICA produces a warning, not a hard block. Complete the FICA items or acknowledge the skip if you continue.

cards.title: Analysis & quotes
questionForms: What happens in Analysis & quotes?
cards.summary: Analysis & quotes is where you record up to three quotes on the case. Quotes are typed records (product type, insurer, premium, commission), not an external insurer integration. You can still move stages if FICA is incomplete; the API returns a warning.

cards.title: Recommendation
questionForms: What happens in Recommendation?
cards.summary: Recommendation is where you select a chosen insurer and estimated commission from the recorded quotes. AdvisorTrack records your selection. It does not recommend a product or insurer for you.

cards.title: Implementation
questionForms: What happens in Implementation?
cards.summary: Implementation is where you submit the case to Production when estimated commission is greater than 0. Submission creates or links a production record (application received, not issued). The case stays open unless you change status separately. Submit also moves the case to Implementation and sets a review due date about 11 months ahead.

cards.title: Review & servicing
questionForms: What happens in Review & servicing?
cards.summary: Review & servicing is the last canonical stage. Schedule Review sets the stage to Review and stores a review due date about 11 months ahead using the backend date calculation. There is no next pipeline stage after Review.

cards.title: Why the API says Interview
questionForms: Why does the API call Fact-finding Interview?
cards.summary: The database and API still store Fact-finding as Interview for Android compatibility. Advisor Workspace always displays Fact-finding. That is a label mapping, not a seventh stage.

cards.title: Move a case to the next stage
questionForms: How do I move a case to the next stage?
cards.summary: Open the case and use Move to stage. The web sends PATCH /cases/:id with currentStage. The backend owns validation and side effects. Drag-and-drop is not used because stage movement must stay an explicit PATCH. Incomplete FICA on later stages returns a warning; it does not return HTTP 400.

cards.title: FICA
questionForms: What is FICA?
cards.summary: FICA on a case is three flags: proof of ID, residence, and bank details. Complete means all three are received. There is also a skip acknowledgement. These are case fields, not uploaded files.

steps.label: Open FICA & Documents on the case

cards.title: Do I have to complete FICA?
questionForms: Do I have to complete FICA?
cards.summary: FICA is expected before Fact-finding and later stages, but incomplete FICA is currently a warning/soft gate, not a hard 400. You can still save the stage change. The warning remains until the three flags are complete or skip is acknowledged.

steps.label: Open FICA & Documents on the case

cards.title: Skip FICA
questionForms: Can I skip FICA?
cards.summary: Yes. Mark skip acknowledged on the case. That is the existing Android/backend acknowledgement, not a desktop-only bypass. Completing the three FICA flags also clears the incomplete warning.

steps.label: Acknowledge skip if you are continuing without the three items

cards.title: Document checklist
questionForms: What are the document checklist items?
cards.summary: Case documents are checklist timestamps, not uploaded files. Default items are Letter of consent, Broker disclosure, and Letter of appointment. Mark sent or received. There is no document vault or file picker on this page.

steps.label: Open FICA & Documents on the case

cards.title: Mark a document as sent
questionForms: How do I mark a document as sent?
cards.summary: Open FICA & Documents and choose Mark sent on the checklist item. That PATCHes the document with markSent and stores a timestamp. It does not upload a file.

cards.title: Mark a document as received
questionForms: How do I mark a document as received?
cards.summary: Open FICA & Documents and choose Mark received. That PATCHes the document with markReceived and stores a timestamp. It does not upload a file.

cards.title: Simple goal
questionForms: What is a simple goal?
cards.summary: Simple goal is one of two fact-find modes (`simple_goal`). Record the product and amount the client described. It does not run financial-planning calculations.

cards.title: Full FNA
questionForms: What is a full FNA?
cards.summary: Full FNA is the other fact-find mode (`full_fna`). It stores the supported needs-analysis fields already on the case (income, expenses, assets, liabilities, risk profile, notes). It does not invent extra planning maths.

cards.title: Quotes
questionForms: How do quotes work?
cards.summary: Quotes are up to three lines on the case: product type, insurer, premium, and commission. Save them with PATCH /cases/:id. Desktop may show them side by side. There is no live insurer feed.

cards.title: How many quotes can I add?
questionForms: How many quotes can I add?
cards.summary: Up to three quotes. The API rejects a fourth quote line. Edit or replace an existing quote instead.

cards.title: Select an insurer
questionForms: How do I select an insurer?
cards.summary: Set chosen insurer on the case (typically from a recorded quote). That stores your selection. AdvisorTrack does not recommend which insurer to choose.

cards.title: Estimated commission
questionForms: What is estimated commission?
cards.summary: Estimated commission is the amount stored on the case. Submit to Production requires it to be greater than 0. Pipeline totals use this field on your open cases. It is not issued production.

cards.title: Set the next action
questionForms: How do I set the next action?
cards.summary: Open Next Action and save a next step date (and time if you set nextStepScheduledAt). The backend upserts a scheduled Activity for that case. The web does not create a second activity in React. After refresh, Activities and Home upcoming show it.

cards.title: Why a next action created an activity
questionForms: Why did setting a next action create an activity?
cards.summary: The case service upserts a scheduled Activity when nextStepDate is saved. That is canonical backend behaviour. You should not add another activity by hand for the same next action.

cards.title: Do I have to set a next action?
questionForms: Do I have to set a next action?
cards.summary: No. Android and the backend allow a case with no next action. Management Needs Attention may flag that. Advisor Workspace encourages a next action visually but does not hard-block save.

cards.title: Submit a case to Production
questionForms: How do I submit a case to Production?
How do I submit to Production?
cards.summary: Open the case, confirm estimated commission and chosen insurer, then Submit to Production. The web PATCHes submitToProduction. The backend creates or links production (application received, not issued) when estimated commission is greater than 0. My Production remains a later page; you will see a placeholder link after success.

steps.label: Confirm estimated commission is greater than 0

cards.title: Why I cannot submit to Production
questionForms: Why can't I submit to Production?
cards.summary: Submit only creates production when estimated commission is greater than 0. If commission is missing or 0, the backend does not submit. Confirm the amount on the case. You also cannot submit a case you do not own.

cards.title: What happens after I submit
questionForms: What happens after I submit?
cards.summary: The backend links or creates a production record, typically application received and not issued, and stores linked production on the case. The case moves to Implementation and a review due date about 11 months ahead is set. The case is not closed by submit.

cards.title: Does submitting close the case?
questionForms: Does submitting close the case?
cards.summary: No. Submit to Production does not set status to closed. Status stays open unless you or an activity outcome changes it (for example Lost).

cards.title: Schedule a review
questionForms: How do I schedule a review?
cards.summary: Open Review and choose Schedule review. That POSTs /cases/:id/schedule-review. The backend sets stage to Review and calculates review due about 11 months ahead. Do not calculate a competing date in the browser.

cards.title: Why review is 11 months ahead
questionForms: Why is review scheduled 11 months ahead?
cards.summary: Schedule review and submit-to-production both add 11 months on the server. That is the existing Android/backend rule, not a web-only date.

cards.title: Duplicate a case
questionForms: How do I duplicate a case?
cards.summary: Duplicate creates a NEW open case for the same contact, starting at Fact-finding (API Interview), copying fact-find fields. It does not copy production. Confirm before you duplicate. There is no delete-case route.

cards.title: What Lost means
questionForms: What does Lost mean?
cards.summary: Lost is a case status. Recording Lost on an activity can also mark a prospect contact inactive and the open case lost. Pipeline shows that after refresh. The web must not mark Lost on its own without the canonical outcome API.

cards.title: Case statuses
questionForms: What do open/won/lost/closed mean?
cards.summary: Cases use only open, won, lost, and closed. Open is in progress. Won is a recorded win. Lost is a recorded loss. Closed is closed without those outcomes. Desktop does not invent extra statuses. There is no delete case.

cards.title: The Assistant is not a financial adviser
questionForms: Can the Assistant recommend a product?
Which insurer should I choose?
cards.summary: The AdvisorTrack Assistant explains product workflow only: stages, FICA, documents, quotes recorded on the case, next actions, and how to submit. It must not recommend a product or insurer, interpret the client’s financial needs, or tell you which policy is best.

cards.title: Add User
questionForms: How do I add a user?
How do I invite a new advisor?
cards.summary: Open Users & Access and choose Add user. Choose the reporting role, region or team when required, and whether to assign a licence. Financial Advisors are invited to Advisor Workspace and the Android app. Leadership and Organisation Administrators are invited to the Management Portal. Assigning a licence needs an Available licence.

steps.label: Complete the person, role, and licence options

cards.title: Organisation Administrator
questionForms: What is an Organisation Administrator?
Is Organisation Admin a role like Team Leader?
cards.summary: Organisation Administrator is a company-scoped grant, not a reporting rank. It is separate from Executive, Regional Manager, Team Leader, and Financial Advisor. Org Admins manage users, licences, Bulk Import, subscription, and invoices. A Financial Advisor who holds this grant may use those portal screens; it does not grant company-wide pipeline, Advisors, Production, or Performance.

cards.title: Resend invitation
questionForms: How do I resend an invitation?
The user did not get the invite email
cards.summary: On Users & Access, open the person and choose Resend invitation. Portal users receive a new activation link for Set up your AdvisorTrack portal account. Financial Advisors receive a mobile invitation. The previous invitation is superseded, not deleted.

cards.title: Deactivate User
questionForms: How do I deactivate a user?
My team leader left
How do I offboard someone?
cards.summary: Use Deactivate User on Users & Access. AdvisorTrack does not hard-delete people. If they had a licence it returns to Available. Reassign their team, region, or reporting line first when they still lead a structure. You cannot deactivate the last Organisation Administrator until another is granted.

steps.label: Reassign Region, Team, or reporting line if they still lead one

cards.title: Reporting-role differences
questionForms: What is the difference between Executive, Regional Manager, and Team Leader?
Why can I only see my team?
cards.summary: Executive sees the company, Regional Manager sees their region, Team Leader sees their team. Financial Advisors do advisor work in Android, not leadership reporting pages. Organisation Admin is a separate grant and does not change this reporting scope. A Team Leader asking for company-wide numbers is limited to their team.

cards.title: Download Excel template
questionForms: How do I download the import template?
Where is the XLSX template?
cards.summary: Open Bulk Import and choose Download Excel Template. Complete the Users to Import sheet only. Download a new template if Regions or Teams have changed. No users are created until you Confirm Import.

steps.label: Complete the Users to Import sheet

cards.title: Upload workbook
questionForms: How do I upload users from Excel?
How do I import a workbook?
cards.summary: On Bulk Import choose Upload Completed Workbook and select the .xlsx file. AdvisorTrack inspects the file, then validates every row on the server. Nothing is created at upload.

cards.title: Validation, preview, and confirm
questionForms: How does bulk import validation work?
When are imported users actually created?
cards.summary: After upload, Bulk Import shows Total rows, Valid, Errors, role counts, and licence demand versus Available. No users, licences, or invitations are created until you click Confirm Import. Failed rows are not left as an unclear half-import. You can download AdvisorTrack User Import Errors.xlsx.

steps.label: Review Valid and Errors on Bulk Import
Fix errors and re-upload if needed

cards.title: Region and Team validation
questionForms: Why did bulk import reject my region or team?
Do region and team names have to match exactly?
cards.summary: Region and Team values must match names that already exist in Regions & Teams. Download a new Excel template after structure changes. A team must belong to the named region. AdvisorTrack re-checks every value on the server.

steps.label: Use the listed Region and Team names

cards.title: Purchased, Assigned, and Available
questionForms: What do Purchased, Assigned and Available mean?
How many licences do we have left?
cards.summary: On Licences, Purchased is the company pool, Assigned is how many people currently have a licence, and Available is Purchased minus Assigned (or Unlimited). Assigning consumes Available. Removing a licence returns it to Available. Purchased only changes after AdvisorTrack confirms additional licences.

cards.title: Assign licence
questionForms: How do I assign a licence?
Why can’t I assign a licence?
cards.summary: Open Licences or Users & Access and choose Assign licence for an unlicensed person. You need Available licences. If Available is 0, request additional licences instead. Assigning does not change Purchased.

cards.title: Remove licence
questionForms: How do I remove a licence?
How do I free up a seat?
cards.summary: On Licences or Users & Access choose Remove licence. The licence returns to Available. The person’s Advisor data is retained. This does not delete the user and does not change Purchased.

cards.title: Request additional licences
questionForms: I need 20 more licences
How do I request additional licences?
I hired 50 new advisors
cards.summary: On Licences choose Add / Request Licences and enter how many extra licences you need. Purchased does not increase until AdvisorTrack confirms the request according to your contract. After confirmation, assign licences and add people via Add user or Bulk Import. Advisors then activate on Android.

steps.label: Choose Add / Request Licences for the shortfall
After confirmation, add people and assign licences

cards.title: Licence pool exhausted
questionForms: No licences available
Why can’t I assign a licence when Available is 0?
cards.summary: When Available is 0, Assign licence is blocked. Request additional licences from Licences, or remove a licence from someone who no longer needs one. Do not exceed the purchased pool.

steps.label: Request additional licences, or Remove licence from someone who no longer needs it

cards.title: Regions
questionForms: How do I manage regions?
Where are Regions & Teams?
cards.summary: Open Regions & Teams (Users & Access with the Regions tab). Executives can create and archive regions and assign a Regional Manager. Regional Managers can view regions. Regions are not deleted; they are archived. Team Leaders do not manage regions.

cards.title: Teams
questionForms: How do I manage teams?
Where do I add a team?
cards.summary: Teams live under Regions & Teams on the Teams tab. A team belongs to a region and has a Team Leader. Team Leaders do not get the Teams tab. Archive a team instead of deleting it.

cards.title: Team Leader relationship
questionForms: My team leader left
How is a Team Leader linked to a team?
cards.summary: Each team has a Team Leader. If a Team Leader leaves, reassign the team to a replacement on Regions & Teams before deactivating them. Reporting scope for the new leader is that team. Historical reporting records are kept.

steps.label: Assign a new Team Leader on the team
Then Deactivate User on the person who left

cards.title: Regional Manager relationship
questionForms: How is a Regional Manager linked to a region?
Who can change the Regional Manager?
cards.summary: Each region has a Regional Manager. Executives assign the Regional Manager on the Regions tab. A Regional Manager sees their region’s teams and advisors. Reassign the region before deactivating a Regional Manager who still holds it.

cards.title: Dashboard
questionForms: What is on the Dashboard?
Where is the overview?
What is Top Performer?
What does Needs Attention mean?
cards.summary: Dashboard is the Management Portal home. Leadership sees issued-performance overview for their reporting scope. Top Performer and the Dashboard Needs Attention card are the highest and lowest issued totals at the comparison rank already used by AdvisorTrack Performance: Executive compares Regional Managers, Regional Manager compares Team Leaders, Team Leader compares Financial Advisors, for Last Week, Last Month, or Year to Date. Advisor details Needs Attention is separate — it uses the product’s canonical reasons (stalled cases, missing documents, no next action, and Last Mobile Activity of 3+ days as Android telemetry, not performance). Organisation Administrators who are not leaders still land here but do not get company-wide pipeline from this page. Figures follow hierarchy scope.

cards.title: Team Pipeline
questionForms: Where is Team Pipeline?
How do I see my team’s cases?
cards.summary: Team Pipeline shows management-scoped client cases. Executives, Regional Managers, and Team Leaders see cases in their reporting line. Organisation Admin does not by itself unlock company-wide pipeline. Open an advisor name to reach advisor details.

cards.title: Advisor details
questionForms: How do I open an advisor’s details?
What does Last Mobile Activity mean?
cards.summary: Open Advisors, or click an advisor name from Team Pipeline, Dashboard, or Production. Last Mobile Activity is Android resource telemetry — when the mobile app last used AdvisorTrack resources. It is not productivity, performance, or attendance. An empty value is not inactivity. Needs Attention on this page uses the same canonical reasons as AdvisorTrack: stalled open cases, missing documents, no next action, and mobile inactivity of 3+ days when Last Mobile Activity is recorded.

cards.title: Production
questionForms: Where is Production?
Where do I see issued commission?
cards.summary: Production shows submitted versus issued commission for advisors in your reporting scope. Leadership uses this page. It is not the same as Performance, and Last Mobile Activity is not a production metric.

cards.title: Performance visibility
questionForms: Why can’t I see Performance?
Where is the Performance page?
cards.summary: In the production Management Portal, Performance is an AdvisorTrack staff page. Customers use Dashboard, Team Pipeline, Advisors, and Production for reporting in their hierarchy scope. On the public demo, leadership can open Performance as a showcase. Last Mobile Activity is not a performance score.

steps.label: Use Production for submitted versus issued commission

cards.title: Performance (public demo)
questionForms: Where is Performance on the demo?
cards.summary: On the public demo, leadership can open Performance from Management. This showcase is not available to customers on the production portal. Last Mobile Activity remains telemetry, not a performance score.

cards.title: Subscription
questionForms: Where is our subscription?
Where do I see our contract?
cards.summary: Organisation Administrators open Subscription to view the organisation’s AdvisorTrack Enterprise contract. Customers can view, not edit, these terms. Additional licences are requested from Licences, not by changing this page.

cards.title: Invoices
questionForms: Where do I find invoices?
How do I download an invoice PDF?
cards.summary: Organisation Administrators open Invoices to view and download invoices for the organisation. Customer users cannot create, send, or void invoices. Invoice numbers start at INV100000 and are never reused. AdvisorTrack does not currently charge VAT.

steps.label: Open an invoice to view or download the PDF

cards.title: AdvisorTrack is not VAT registered
questionForms: Why is there no VAT on my invoice?
Is AdvisorTrack VAT registered?
cards.summary: AdvisorTrack is not currently registered for VAT. Invoices show VAT not charged. They must not add VAT, imply VAT included, or print an AdvisorTrack VAT number. This is AdvisorTrack’s seller status, not a setting you change on Subscription.

steps.label: Open Invoices to view the VAT not charged label

cards.title: Why can’t I see this page?
questionForms: Why can’t I see this page?
Why is a menu item missing?
cards.summary: The Management Portal only shows pages your rank, Organisation Admin grant, and permissions allow. Ordinary Financial Advisors use Advisor Workspace for their own book, not leadership reporting pages. A Financial Advisor who is also Organisation Administrator may see organisation/account administration only. Team Leaders see their team, not the company. Some commercial pages are Organisation Admin only. Ask your Organisation Administrator, or contact AdvisorTrack support.

cards.title: Why can’t I assign a licence?
questionForms: Why can’t I assign a licence?
The Assign licence button is disabled
cards.summary: Licence assignment is done on Licences or Users & Access by an Organisation Administrator (or someone with member-management permission). If you can open Licences but Assign licence is blocked, Available is 0 — request additional licences or remove an unused licence. Purchased does not change until AdvisorTrack confirms extra licences.

steps.label: Open Licences if you manage licences

cards.title: Why can’t I import users?
questionForms: Why can’t I import users?
Where is Bulk Import?
cards.summary: Bulk Import is for Organisation Administrators, platform staff, or users with manage_members. Leadership access alone is not enough. If you do not see Bulk Import, ask your Organisation Administrator to import the workbook or grant the right access.

steps.label: Ask your Organisation Administrator, or open Bulk Import if you have it

cards.title: Why can’t I see Performance?
questionForms: Why can’t I see Performance?
Why is Performance missing from the menu?
cards.summary: On portal.advisortrack.co.za, Performance is AdvisorTrack staff-only. Use Dashboard, Team Pipeline, Advisors, and Production instead. On the public demo, leadership can open Performance. Last Mobile Activity is Android telemetry, not a performance rating.

cards.title: I can’t add a contact
questionForms: I can’t add a contact
cards.summary: If Add Contact is blocked, check the API reason. First name plus email or phone is required. LIVE_PREVIEW_REQUIRED means enable Live Preview or upgrade to Pro. CONTACT_LIMIT_REACHED means you already have 3 active real contacts on Live Preview. Are you missing email/phone, or did the page mention Live Preview or a contact limit?

cards.title: I can’t edit this contact
questionForms: I can’t edit this contact
cards.summary: If Edit is blocked, the API usually returns CONTACT_ARCHIVED or LIVE_PREVIEW_REQUIRED. Archived real contacts are read-only on free/Live Preview until you activate a slot or upgrade to Pro. Practice contacts stay editable. Are you looking at an archived real contact, or did Live Preview need to be enabled?

cards.title: My contact disappeared
questionForms: My contact disappeared
cards.summary: Contacts are self-scoped. A URL for another advisor’s contact looks like “not in your book” and does not reveal that it exists. Search only matches name and company. Archived real contacts still appear in your list, marked Archived. On the public demo, Reset Demo restores the canonical Maya book. Did you search by email/phone, open someone else’s link, or reset the demo?

cards.title: I reached the contact limit
questionForms: I reached the contact limit
cards.summary: Live Preview allows 3 active real contacts. Practice contacts are not counted. Activate an archived contact to swap the oldest active slot, or upgrade to Pro for unlimited real contacts. This is not a company licence seat limit. Did the message say CONTACT_LIMIT_REACHED, or were you trying to import on a non-Pro plan?

cards.title: Import isn’t working
questionForms: Import isn’t working
cards.summary: Advisor contact import needs Pro (IMPORT_PRO_REQUIRED), 1–50 rows, first name plus email or phone on each row, and consentAccepted true. It is structured rows, not an XLSX company user workbook. Duplicates are counted, not overwritten. Are you on Pro, and did you confirm POPIA consent for advisor contacts rather than company Bulk Import?

cards.title: Why did this contact become inactive?
questionForms: Why did this contact become inactive?
cards.summary: Inactive may result from an activity outcome of Lost. That is contact status, not Live Preview archive. If the contact is Archived instead, an active Live Preview slot was swapped or the plan archived excess real contacts. Was the status Inactive, or was the activation state Archived?

cards.title: Why did this prospect become a client?
questionForms: Why did this prospect become a client?
cards.summary: Client is set when production income for that contact is recognised or issued. It is not a “converted” status you invent in Contacts. If the status is still Prospect, issued production has not been recognised for them yet.

cards.title: I can't create an activity
questionForms: I can't create an activity
cards.summary: Title, type, and a valid scheduled date and time are required. Type must be one of call, meeting, email, follow_up, presentation, or other. Contact is optional. If the contact ID is not in your book, the API returns not found without saying whether another advisor has that person. Check the form values first, then retry. You cannot create an activity for another advisor.

cards.title: I can't complete this activity
questionForms: I can't complete this activity
Why can't I proceed?
cards.summary: An outcome can be recorded only once. If the activity is already completed with an outcome, the API returns OUTCOME_EXISTS. Proceed at Review has no next stage and returns NO_NEXT_STAGE. Out-of-scope IDs return not found. If you meant Complete instead of Proceed, Complete does not create a next activity.

cards.title: My follow-up disappeared
questionForms: My follow-up disappeared
cards.summary: Check the Today, Upcoming, Overdue, and Completed tabs — a completed activity leaves Today. If it was deleted, the current API permanently removes it and it cannot be restored. Reset Demo on the public demo restores Maya’s canonical activities. You cannot see another advisor’s activity even if you guess the ID.

cards.title: Why was a new activity created?
questionForms: Why was a new activity created?
Why did my case stage change?
cards.summary: Proceed creates the next activity at the next pipeline stage and updates the open case to that stage. Complete only advances the case if you chose advanceCase. The web does not invent a second activity. If you did not choose Proceed, ask whether someone else on this demo session recorded an outcome.

cards.title: I picked Lost by mistake
questionForms: I picked Lost by mistake
cards.summary: Lost already marked the related prospect Inactive and the open case lost. Current product does not offer an undo. You can add a new activity later, but the Lost outcome stays on the original activity. On the public demo, Reset Demo restores canonical Maya data.

steps.label: Open the contact if you still have it

cards.title: My activity is showing overdue
questionForms: My activity is showing overdue
cards.summary: Overdue means the scheduled date and time is already past and the status is still scheduled. Africa/Johannesburg is used. Complete, Proceed, Lost, or reschedule the time if it should no longer be outstanding.

cards.title: I can't move this case
questionForms: I can't move this case
cards.summary: Stage movement uses PATCH /cases/:id and only works on a case you own. If the case is lost or closed, it will not sit in an open pipeline column. Incomplete FICA shows a warning but does not block the save. If this is not your case, you cannot open it. Are you trying to move an open case you own, or is the case already lost/closed?

cards.title: I can't submit to Production
questionForms: I can't submit to Production
cards.summary: Submit requires estimated commission greater than 0 on this case. If the amount is 0 or blank, the backend does not create production. Confirm you own the case. Already submitted cases keep their linked production; submitting again updates that draft rather than inventing a second book. Is estimated commission greater than 0?

cards.title: My FICA warning won't go away
questionForms: My FICA warning won't go away
cards.summary: The warning stays until proof of ID, residence, and bank are all received, or skip is acknowledged. It is a warning, not a 400. Mark the three flags or acknowledge skip, then save.

steps.label: Complete the three items or acknowledge skip

cards.title: I can't add another quote
questionForms: I can't add another quote
cards.summary: A case may have at most three quotes. Edit or replace one of the existing three. There is no extra quote slot and no insurer integration.

cards.title: Why is this case Lost?
questionForms: Why is this case Lost?
cards.summary: Lost is a case status. Recording Lost on an activity sets the open case to lost and can mark a prospect contact inactive. Pipeline shows that after refresh. There is no undo. On the public demo, Reset Demo restores canonical Maya data. Did you record Lost on an activity for this contact?

cards.title: Why did my contact become inactive?
questionForms: Why did my contact become inactive?
cards.summary: Lost on an activity can set a prospect contact to inactive as well as the open case to lost. That is backend behaviour, not a separate Contacts action. If the contact was already a client, ask whether status was changed on the contact form instead.

cards.title: My next action created an activity
questionForms: My next action created an activity
cards.summary: Saving nextStepDate upserts a scheduled Activity on the server. That is expected. Do not create a second activity in React for the same next action. After refresh it appears on Activities and Home upcoming.

cards.title: I can't find my case
questionForms: I can't find my case
cards.summary: Pipeline lists only your own cases. Another advisor’s case returns not found. Filter by stage or status, or open the contact and choose Open Case — that get-or-creates the open case for that contact. Lost cases still exist but are not open. Are you looking in your own Pipeline, or opening a case id from another book?

steps.label: Or open the contact and choose Open Case

cards.title: Why is this case still open after submitting?
questionForms: Why is this case still open after submitting?
cards.summary: Submitting to Production does not close the case. Status stays open, stage becomes Implementation, and production is linked as not issued. Close or win the case only if you change status through the existing case fields — not as an automatic submit side effect.

cards.title: My review date looks wrong
questionForms: My review date looks wrong
cards.summary: Schedule review and submit-to-production both set review due about 11 months ahead on the server from today’s date. The web does not calculate a second date. If you scheduled again, the backend recalculates from now. Check whether you scheduled review or submitted, rather than typing a date locally.

steps.label: Schedule review again if you need a fresh 11-month date

cards.title: Licence
questionForms: What is a licence?
Is a seat the same as a licence?
cards.summary: A licence is a purchased AdvisorTrack seat assigned to a person. Purchased is the pool, Assigned is in use, Available is what you can still assign. “Seats” in conversation means licences.

cards.title: Organisation Administrator
questionForms: What does Organisation Administrator mean?
cards.summary: A company-scoped grant for users, licences, Bulk Import, subscription, and invoices. It is not a reporting rank and does not replace Executive, Regional Manager, Team Leader, or Financial Advisor. A Financial Advisor who holds it may use those portal screens; it does not grant leadership reporting.

cards.title: Financial Advisor
questionForms: What is a Financial Advisor in AdvisorTrack?
cards.summary: The customer rank that does advisor work in Advisor Workspace (/advisor) and the Android app. Organisation Admin is a separate grant and may allow organisation/account administration in the portal; it does not grant leadership reporting. Advisor work appears to leadership through Team Pipeline, Advisors, and Production.

cards.title: Last Mobile Activity
questionForms: What is Last Mobile Activity?
Does Last Mobile Activity mean the advisor is productive?
cards.summary: Last Mobile Activity is Android resource telemetry. It shows when the mobile app last used AdvisorTrack resources. It must never be described as productivity, performance, or attendance. An empty value is not inactivity — the field may still be empty.

cards.title: Organisation Administrator required
questionForms: I do not have Organisation Admin access
cards.summary: This action is for your Organisation Administrator (or AdvisorTrack staff). Organisation Admin is a company grant, not a reporting rank. Ask your Organisation Administrator, or contact AdvisorTrack support. The assistant will not describe internal staff tools.

cards.title: Financial Advisors use Advisor Workspace
questionForms: Can a Financial Advisor use the portal?
cards.summary: Financial Advisors do their own book in Advisor Workspace (/advisor) and in the Android app. They do not use Management Portal leadership reporting (Team Pipeline, Advisors, company Production, Performance). A Financial Advisor who is also Organisation Administrator may switch to organisation/account administration; that grant is not leadership scope.

cards.title: Scope limited to your team
questionForms: Why can I only see my team?
cards.summary: Team Leaders see their own team. Reporting scope is hierarchy-controlled and resolved on the server. Organisation Admin does not expand pipeline or production to the whole company. Ask your Regional Manager or Executive for a wider view.

cards.title: Scope limited to your region
questionForms: Why can I only see my region?
cards.summary: Regional Managers see their region. Company-wide reporting belongs to Executives. Organisation Admin does not replace reporting rank. Ask your Executive if you need a company view.

cards.title: AdvisorTrack staff only
questionForms: Why is this an internal page?
cards.summary: This is an AdvisorTrack staff tool, not a customer page. Use the customer screens in your menu, or contact AdvisorTrack support. The assistant does not describe internal approval queues or engineering tools to customers.

cards.title: Not available in the public demo
questionForms: Why is this missing on the demo?
cards.summary: Some AdvisorTrack staff tools are production-only and are not in the public demo. The demo uses isolated Northstar data. Emails and payments are simulated. Customer portal features stay in parity with production.

cards.title: Reset Demo
questionForms: How do I reset the demo?
What does Reset Demo do?
cards.summary: On the public demo, Reset Demo restores the isolated Northstar workspace. It is a demo-only control in the top bar. It does not affect production AdvisorTrack customers.

steps.label: Choose Reset Demo in the demo top bar

cards.title: Viewing as
questionForms: What does Viewing as do?
How do I switch demo roles?
cards.summary: Viewing as is the public-demo role switcher in the top bar. It lets you look at the portal as Executive, Regional Manager, Team Leader, or Organisation Admin. It is demo-only and is not how production users change identity.

steps.label: Use Viewing as in the demo top bar

cards.title: Simulated emails and payments
questionForms: Will the demo send a real email?
Are demo payments real?
cards.summary: On the public demo, invitation emails and payments are simulated. Nothing is billed and no live customer mailbox is contacted. Production sends real activation email and records real invoices.

cards.title: Demo badge
questionForms: What is the AdvisorTrack Demo badge?
How do I know I am on the demo?
cards.summary: The AdvisorTrack Demo pill in the sidebar marks the public demo portal. Production at portal.advisortrack.co.za does not show this badge.

cards.title: Enterprise Customers
questionForms: Where is enterprise customer onboarding?
cards.summary: Internal AdvisorTrack onboarding for new enterprise customers. Not a customer portal page. Do not describe this workflow to customer sessions.

cards.title: Internal licence request queue
questionForms: Where do staff confirm additional licences?
cards.summary: Internal queue where AdvisorTrack staff review customer additional-licence requests. Customers request from Licences; they never use this page. Do not describe the queue to customer sessions.

cards.title: Engineering Change Log
questionForms: Where is the Engineering Change Log?
cards.summary: Internal Engineering Change Log. Never exposed on the public demo. Not a customer feature.

cards.title: Platform company administration
questionForms: Where do staff administer companies?
cards.summary: Internal Companies, customer account, and Subscriptions administration. Production-only staff surfaces. The public demo Company Details page is a customer showcase and is not this tool.
